title: The Fall of Constantinople, 1453
summary: For 53 days Sultan Mehmed II besieged the last great city of the Byzantine Empire. Giant cannons, ships dragged over a hill and a final dawn assault ended an empire that had lasted over 1,000 years.

events.title: The siege begins
events.text: Mehmed II's army surrounds the land walls of the city.

events.title: The great chain
events.text: A huge chain across the Golden Horn blocks Ottoman ships from the city's harbour.

events.title: Bombardment of the walls
events.text: Orban's giant cannon fires stone balls weighing over 500 kg at the Theodosian Walls.

events.title: Genoese ships break through
events.text: Four Christian ships fight their way past the Ottoman fleet into the harbour.

events.title: Ships over the hill
events.text: About 70 galleys are dragged on greased logs over the hill behind Galata, around the chain and into the Golden Horn.

events.title: The final assault
events.text: Wave after wave attacks the walls near the Gate of St Romanus. Emperor Constantine XI dies fighting.

events.title: Mehmed enters Hagia Sophia
events.text: The great church becomes a mosque. Constantinople becomes the Ottoman capital.

story.title: The last Roman city
story.text: By 1453 the once-mighty **Byzantine Empire** – the eastern half of the Roman Empire – had shrunk to little more than its capital, **Constantinople**. The young Ottoman sultan **Mehmed II** was determined to take it.

question.prompt: The Byzantine Empire was the continuation of which earlier empire?

story.title: Walls against cannons
story.text: Constantinople's **Theodosian Walls** had stopped every attacker for 1,000 years. But Mehmed brought something new: huge **gunpowder cannons**, including one built by the engineer Orban.

question.prompt: What new weapon made the walls vulnerable?

story.title: Ships over a hill
story.text: A giant chain blocked the **Golden Horn** harbour. So on 22 April Mehmed had about **70 ships dragged over land** on greased logs, behind the Genoese colony of Galata, and launched them inside the harbour.

story.title: The final assault
story.text: Before dawn on **29 May 1453** the Ottomans attacked in waves. Defenders held until a small gate was left open and the walls were breached. **Emperor Constantine XI** died in the fighting.

story.title: A new capital
story.text: Mehmed rode to **Hagia Sophia** and turned the great church into a mosque. Constantinople (later **Istanbul**) became the Ottoman capital. Many historians use 1453 to mark the **end of the Middle Ages**.

question.prompt: Why is 1453 often seen as a turning point?
choices: It ended the Byzantine Empire and is often used to mark the end of the Middle Ages
It was the year gunpowder was invented

sources: Steven Runciman, The Fall of Constantinople 1453 (1965)
Roger Crowley, 1453: The Holy War for Constantinople and the Clash of Islam and the West (2005)
